title: The naive framing: "just faster content"
text: People assume the marketing plugin is just a faster way to get content written. It isn't. It plans, analyzes, and refines like a collaborator would. So, what does it actually change? If

title: You're already doing marketing
text: You're running a business, you're running marketing, whether or not you'd call yourself a marketer. Content needs making, campaigns need planning, competitors need watching. Somewhere in the middle, you decide what to say to whom and where.

title: More than a drafting tool
text: Most tools stop at write me a blog post. This one plans, analyzes, and refines. It understands strategy, not just content generation. The alternative is the brief you scroll between meetings, half a thought handed to whoever's free. A collaborator that already knows your brand changes that math. Five

title: Five sides, one install
text: Capabilities come under one install: creating content, planning campaigns, reading competitors, interpreting performance, and holding your brand consistent. Not five apps, five sides of one collaborator. Content creation isn't

title: Content creation
text: Just write me a post. It's structured development briefs, outlines, drafts, and variations. Email sequences, social calendars, landing page copy, ad variants, each shaped by your configured voice and audience. Campaign planning

title: Campaign planning
text: Runs from the initial brief to channel strategy. Tell it what you're launching, who you're reaching, and what you want them to do. It helps build the messaging framework, choose channels, and plan the execution.

title: Reads the competition
text: It also watches the competition, how rivals position themselves, who they're talking to, what they claim. Then it finds the gap, the angle everyone's ignoring, the audience nobody's addressing. Connect your analytics and

title: Reads the numbers with you
text: It reads the campaign data with you. Not just here are the numbers, here's what the numbers suggest you do next. Interpretation, not another dashboard. And it holds the line on brand.

title: Holds the brand line
text: Configure your voice, tone, and terminology once, and it enforces them across everything it produces, which matters most exactly when you're shipping volume and consistency starts to slip. Out of the box, it works, but

title: The setup that pays for itself
text: The real gain hides in customization, and customization is three inputs: your brand voice, your audience, and what you actually sell.

title: The anchor: specificity is the lever
text: Specificity is the lever. "Professionals" is nearly useless. Small business owners considering AI tools, but not technical, that's something it can aim at. The narrower you describe the target, the sharper everything downstream.

title: Voice, calibrated by example
text: Voice is calibrated by example, not description. Show it a few paragraphs you've written in your tone and tell it who you're reaching. It calibrates to that, not to a generic house style.

title: The anchor returns — fifteen minutes
text: 50 minutes of this changes the output. Content comes back closer to your voice, ideas grounded in your real business, competitive analysis focused on the players who actually matter. 80% trite on the first draft beats 50% trite by a lot. Instead of staring at a blank

title: The content calendar
text: Month, say, "Build me a calendar, two posts a week, a weekly newsletter, two blog pieces for this audience on these themes." It returns a structured calendar with a specific idea in every slot. You're editing a plan, not inventing one.

title: The email sequence
text: Say you're launching a new service next month. Ask for a five-email sequence aimed at subscribers who know you, but have never bought anything. It drafts the whole arc, subject lines, body copy, and calls to action, each email building on the one before. You add the personal anecdotes it can't know, and the sequence is ready to load. Repurposing is the tedious work everyone

title: Repurposing
text: Skips. One long blog post becomes five social posts, a newsletter intro, and a short video script from a single source. This is where it saves real hours. And the monthly reckoning, which pieces

title: The monthly reckoning
text: Landed, which fell flat, is there a pattern? Feed it your metrics, and it goes past the numbers to what they mean for next month's strategy. Across all five workflows, the shift is the same. You're editing a plan, not staring at a blank page. Four habits separate the people who get

title: Four habits
text: Value from the people who get slop. Front-load your brand configuration, ask for variations, delegate the formats you hate, and review everything. Everyone has formats they dread: captions, subject lines, meta descriptions. Hand those over specifically, and keep your creative energy for the work only you can do. Ask

title: Options, not answers
text: For options, not answers. Give me five angles on this headline beats write me a headline almost every time. The plugin is at its best producing a spread you choose from, not one guess. But review everything that goes public.

title: What it won't do
text: It drafts well, your touch is what makes the work yours. It won't replace your CMO, it just means you're never again starting from a brief scrolled between meetings. You keep the judgment, it takes the grind.

title: Carry-out
text: The marketing plugin turns Claude from a content generator into a collaborator. It plans, watches competitors, and reads your numbers with you. But it only gets specific once you do, and the judgment stays yours.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn, paste this into Claude. I just installed the marketing plugin before drafting anything, interview me. Ask for a few paragraphs I've written so you can learn my voice. Ask who my audience is and push me to get specific. Ask what I sell and what makes it different. Then hand me back a short brand config to save and name the first campaign we should build. That's the 50 minutes this whole video is about. Run it before you ask for a single draft.

title: Outro
text: Claude on message, the marketing plugin. Liam in for Bear.
